title: Kasa Syntax Practice Workbook
edition: Phase 4B · three runnable cases per chapter
method: Predict → trace → execute → change → explain. Worked examples are not grades; independent transfer is the goal.

units.chapter: Writing Kasa source: lines, comments and names
units.objective: A computer cannot guess your instructions. Learn exactly what counts as a statement, comment and identifier.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma din = "Ama"
ka din
ma din = "Kofi"
ka din
newExample.purpose: Trace two successive assignments to the same name.
newExample.coach: Only ka prints. The second ma changes what din refers to.
newExample.transfer: Rename din to name on every line; predict whether the output changes.

debugging.explanation: Names are case-sensitive: School and school are different. Use the assigned spelling.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern # comment without reading the worked answer.
Replace ɛdin with name in both statements. What happens if you replace it in only one?
Rewrite the fresh example using different meaningful identifier names, while keeping its output unchanged.
checklist: I can predict the output before running.
I can trace which values change and why.
I can intentionally cause and explain a mistake.
I can solve a modified version without copying.

units.chapter: The types: numbers, strings, Boolean and hwee
units.objective: Different kinds of information follow different rules; knowing the type prevents surprising mistakes.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ka 12
ka "12"
ka nokware
ka atoro
newExample.purpose: Distinguish numeric, text and Boolean values even when display is similar.
newExample.coach: The first 12 and second "12" look identical but have different types.
newExample.transfer: Try ka nɔma("12") + 3 and explain the conversion.

debugging.explanation: Conditions require Boolean, not number. Write sɛ nokware a for a deliberately true branch.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern 42 | 2.5 | "text" | nokware | atoro | hwee without reading the worked answer.
What are the types of 12, "12", nokware, atoro and hwee? Which can be used in arithmetic without conversion?

units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma mfe = 17
ka mfe >= 18
ka mfe < 18
newExample.purpose: Explain the inclusive and exclusive age comparisons.
newExample.coach: 17 is not at least 18 but is less than 18.
newExample.transfer: Try mfe = 18 and then 19; explain which comparison changes.

debugging.explanation: Chaining comparisons directly is unsupported; use (1 < 2) ne (2 < 3).

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern ==  !=  <  <=  >  >= without reading the worked answer.
For scores 49, 50 and 51, predict >= 50, > 50 and == 50. Build a truth table.

units.chapter: Boolean logic: ne, anaa and ɛnyɛ
units.objective: Sometimes more than one condition matters: permission may require two rules or allow alternatives.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma mfe = 20
ma wɔ_kaad = nokware
ka mfe >= 18 ne wɔ_kaad
ka ɛnyɛ wɔ_kaad
newExample.purpose: Predict the combination of two true conditions and negation.
newExample.coach: AND is true only when both inputs are true. NOT inverts a Boolean.
newExample.transfer: Change wɔ_kaad to atoro and predict both lines.

debugging.explanation: Use strict Boolean operands such as nokware ne nokware, not numeric truthiness.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern COND ne COND | COND anaa COND | ɛnyɛ COND without reading the worked answer.
Draw all four combinations for A and B. Calculate A ne B and A anaa B for each.

units.objective: A conditional selects one of two paths based on a Boolean result.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma sɔhwɛ = 72
sɛ sɔhwɛ >= 50 a
    ka "Pass"
anyɛ_saa_a
    ka "Review"
awiei
newExample.purpose: Follow the branch chosen by a comparison.
newExample.coach: Only one of the two branches prints; awiei closes the block.
newExample.transfer: Test sɔhwɛ = 49 and exactly 50. Explain the difference.

debugging.explanation: The required a is missing: sɛ score >= 50 a.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern sɛ CONDITION a ... [anyɛ_saa_a ...] awiei without reading the worked answer.

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation

mpɛn 4
    ma sika = sika + 10
awiei
ka sika
newExample.coach: The variable changes four times but is printed only after the loop.
newExample.transfer: Change the count to three and contribution to twelve.

debugging.explanation: The repeat count must be a nonnegative integer.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern mpɛn COUNT ... awiei without reading the worked answer.
Trace total for five repetitions of +4, writing down the value after each pass.

units.objective: Use a while loop when you cannot know in advance how many times a task will repeat.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma n = 1
bere_a n <= 4
    ka n
    ma n = n + 1
awiei
newExample.purpose: Trace the loop condition and update on each iteration.
newExample.coach: When n becomes 5, the loop condition is false and the body stops.
newExample.transfer: Replace <= with < and predict the last number.

debugging.incorrect:
ma n = 1
bere_a n <= 3
    ka n
awiei
debugging.explanation: The counter never changes, so the loop does not naturally stop. Update n in the body.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern bere_a CONDITION ... awiei without reading the worked answer.
Modify the counter so the loop prints 2, 4, 6 and 8 without printing 10.

units.chapter: Break and continue: gyae and toa_so
units.objective: Sometimes a loop should stop early or skip one pass when a condition is met.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma n = 0
mpɛn 5
    ma n = n + 1
    sɛ n == 3 a
        gyae
    awiei
    ka n
awiei
newExample.purpose: Identify the moment gyae exits the loop.
newExample.coach: The third iteration breaks before ka n.
newExample.transfer: Change n == 3 to n == 4; identify how many values print.

debugging.explanation: gyae only makes sense inside an active loop; put it in a loop conditional.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern gyae | toa_so (inside loops) without reading the worked answer.
Show how the output changes when gyae is replaced with toa_so. Why must the increment happen first?

units.objective: Write a calculation once, call it with several values and reuse the returned result.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
dwumadie bom(a, b)
    sanma a + b
awiei
ka bom(4, 5)
ka bom(2, 8)
newExample.purpose: Trace two calls to the same function with different arguments.
newExample.coach: sanma returns a result; ka outside prints it.
newExample.transfer: Change the function name to add everywhere, then call it with different inputs.

debugging.incorrect:
dwumadie total(qty, price)
    ka qty * price
awiei
ka total(3, 7)
debugging.explanation: ka inside the function prints, but without sanma the function returns hwee. Use sanma for a reusable result.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern dwumadie NAME(PARAMS) ... sanma EXPR ... awiei without reading the worked answer.
Write a function that adds a fixed fee to a base price, then call it with two different amounts.

units.chapter: Lists: brackets, zero-based indexing and length
units.objective: Organize several related values without inventing a new variable name for each one.
units.preflight: Before running: mark every fixed Kasa keyword, underline the learner-chosen names, and write the exact output (including labels and line breaks).

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma nsɔhwɛ = [70, 80, 90]
ka nsɔhwɛ[0]
ka nsɔhwɛ[2]
ka tentɛn(nsɔhwɛ)
newExample.purpose: Connect zero-based indexes to list length.
newExample.coach: Index 0 is the first item. The list contains three items.
newExample.transfer: Try index 1, then deliberately request index 3 and read the error.

debugging.explanation: With three entries, only 0, 1 and 2 are valid indices. Position 3 does not exist.

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern [EXPR, EXPR] | LIST[INDEX] | tentɛn(LIST) without reading the worked answer.
Create a list of four scores; print its second value, last value and length.

units.chapter: Built-ins: bisa, tentɛn, nɔma and nsɛm

newExample.title: Apply the rule in a fresh situation
newExample.code:
ma sika = 46
ka "Total GHS: " + nsɛm(sika)
ka tentɛn([5, 10, 15])
newExample.purpose: Explain converting numbers to text and finding list length.
newExample.coach: nsɛm makes a numeric result usable with a string label; tentɛn returns the number of elements.
newExample.transfer: Remove nsɛm and read the error, then restore it.

debugging.explanation: The input text is not a valid numeric representation. Use a numeric string such as "5".

mastery: Explain the syntax pattern bisa([PROMPT]) | tentɛn(TEXT_OR_LIST) | nɔma(TEXT) | nsɛm(VALUE) without reading the worked answer.
